name: Which Place Looks Safer? Human Anchor Set for LLM Comparison
description: Rebuilt from the published description of Zhang, Li, Fukuda & Wang (2025). Participants read the paper's basic safety criteria (9 safe and 11 dangerous cues) and then answer "Which place looks safer?" for pairs of Osaka street views, or choose "Cannot compare". In the paper these human votes formed the anchor set used to test whether multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o and others) judge safety like people. The paper scores each image as wins minus losses (+1 safer, 0 cannot compare, −1 less safe); the platform shows TrueSkill, and the export has every vote for the paper's score. Differences from the original study: (1) The paper does not say how many pairs each volunteer judged; here each participant judges 30 pairs. (2) The paper's main anchor set was 1,000 Chengdu images (Baidu); its Osaka comparison set used Google Street View. Bundled images are 64 Google Street View views from random points in Osaka (2018–2026), one compass direction each, not the original set. (3) The age bands follow the sample the paper reports; "Over 65" and the gender option "Other / prefer not to say" are additions.
author: Zhang, Li, Fukuda & Wang
